method: Every failure was traced to the earliest pipeline stage that lost the information, by materialising each intermediate representation in turn (upload validation -> source selection -> OCR pages -> rows -> candidates -> normalisation -> validation) rather than inferring from the final output.

findings.title: Every image upload was processed to nothing
findings.root_cause: Source selection enumerated the pages needing OCR from the PDF text-extraction result. A non-PDF upload never appears in that list, so the OCR branch was never entered.
findings.evidence: R2-02/R2-03/R2-06 finished processing_status=COMPLETED in 5.5-6.9 ms with zero OCRResult rows, document_type=UNKNOWN and no extracted fields. PaddleOCR was never invoked.
findings.regression: Introduced by the previous round's per-page routing change. At 2228b75 the document-level gate sent any non-PDF to the OCR branch.
findings.fix: services/processing.py -- a non-PDF upload is one page that only OCR can read.

findings.title: A checklist could switch off the missing-field safety net
findings.root_cause: validate_document replaced the default missing-field net with the configured rule list whenever that list was non-empty. When no configured rule was executable at document scope the engine emitted zero issues, and overall_status defaulted to READY.
findings.evidence: R2-01, R2-04 and R2-07 all reported overall_status=READY while missing_expected_fields was non-empty and every field the type needs was unresolved. Both seeded workflows configure only DATE_COMPARISON / NUMERIC_COMPARISON, which are submission-scope rule types with no document-scope handler.
findings.fix: validation/engine.py -- only a REQUIRED_FIELD rule may redefine what 'required' means; any other rule list leaves the net in place.

findings.title: Typographic dashes silently voided numbers and dates
findings.root_cause: The date and business-number patterns accepted only ASCII hyphen and space. Recognizers emit U+2013 for a typographic hyphen, and NFKC does not fold it.
findings.evidence: R2-06 was OCR'd with 430 characters at mean confidence 0.867 and every field was resolvable in the recognised text -- '사업자등록번호:[REDACTED_BUSINESS_REGISTRATION_NUMBER]' and '유효기간: 2021-04-01 ~ 2022-03-31' -- yet no field was produced, because every separator was U+2013.
findings.fix: normalization/field_normalizer.py -- canonicalize_numeric_text folds the dash family; extraction text normalisation uses the same function.

findings.title: A label box ending on its colon discarded the whole row
findings.root_cause: When the label matched at its own segment end with an empty remainder, candidate generation treated it as 'no value on this row' and abandoned the segment walk instead of looking at the next box on the same visual row.
findings.evidence: R2-06 rows '기업명:' + '[REDACTED_COMPANY_NAME]', '대표자명:' + '[REDACTED_REPRESENTATIVE_NAME]' and '유효기간:' + '<range>' each produced no candidate, although every value was present and correctly recognised.
findings.fix: extraction/base.py -- an empty remainder after a colon now falls through to the same later-segment path already used for a label with no separator.

findings.title: The issue date was unreachable because certificates never label it
findings.root_cause: Issue-date extraction required a 발급일/발급일자/발행일자 label. The certificate types in scope print the issue date as a bare line in the issuance block.
findings.evidence: R2-02, R2-04, R2-05, R2-06 and R2-07 all print the issue date unlabelled; all five were unresolved.
findings.fix: extraction/base.py -- standalone_date_candidate, gated on the bare date being unique across the document AND followed on the same page by a row naming an issuer.
findings.rejected_alternative: Uniqueness alone was tried first and is not sufficient: a lone date in a transcript body is not an issue date, and an existing test pins exactly that.

findings.title: WEBP certificates could not be uploaded at all
findings.root_cause: The upload allowlist covered only pdf/png/jpg/jpeg. Even once admitted, PaddleOCR reads a fixed suffix set and cannot open .webp.
findings.evidence: R2-05 was rejected with INVALID_FILE_TYPE (400) before any processing. After the allowlist change it reached OCR and returned OCR_EMPTY_RESULT because of the codec.
findings.fix: services/storage/local.py -- RIFF/WEBP signature; preprocessing/processor.py -- transcode to PNG before OCR when the codec is not one the engine reads.

findings.title: ImagePreprocessor was dead code
findings.root_cause: The class existed with zero callers, and it rewrote the stored file in place, which made it unsafe to wire in as written.
findings.decision: Refactored into conditional preparation rather than wired in wholesale: EXIF orientation (which the OCR loader ignores entirely) and codec, both applied only when actually needed, writing a copy so stored bytes and the upload checksum are untouched. Deskew and contrast work was rejected: no document in either real-document round showed skew worth correcting.

findings.title: Dense table headers merge across columns, and one OCR box hides two labels
findings.root_cause: On R2-04 the detector emitted a single box '학성' at height 88 px where every neighbouring box was 42-45 px, spanning two physical text lines and straddling two table columns. Row grouping then merged the two lines into one row, so 학번 and 성명 were interleaved and neither label existed as a contiguous string.
findings.why_not_fixed: The information needed to recover this -- which column the character 학 belongs to -- is destroyed inside the box. No downstream stage can reconstruct it, and any rule that guessed would be inventing a mapping. A layout/table model is the principled remedy; it is not a bug fix and is not attempted here.

findings.title: Seal occlusion hides the issuing institution
findings.root_cause: The official stamp overlaps the signature line, so the last character of the issuer is misread or dropped ('경북대학교 총장' recognised as '경 북 대 학교 총 려니'). Shape validation then rejects the surviving fragment, correctly.
findings.effect: university_name unresolved on R2-04 and R2-07 (both PARTIAL ground truth: only a letter-spaced signature block carries the name).

findings.title: A 743x1020 JPEG misreads one Hangul syllable in a personal name
findings.root_cause: R2-03 was recognised at mean confidence 0.910 with student_name read as a different surname. Shape validation cannot detect this: the value is a plausible Hangul personal name of legal length.
findings.effect: The single wrong non-null value in the round. It is reported, not hidden: confidence 0.917, evidence assessment SUFFICIENT, and the field still carries its raw OCR text so a reviewer can see the recognizer's output.

findings.title: Project-level verification can be READY while a document is REVIEW_REQUIRED
findings.root_cause: Submission verification only evaluates the rules a workflow configures. The seeded student workflow references issue_date but not university_name or student_id, so unread fields are invisible to it, while the document-level status correctly reports REVIEW_REQUIRED.
findings.evidence: R2-05 and R2-07: document overall_status=REVIEW_REQUIRED with unread university_name, project verification=READY.
findings.why_not_fixed: Changing what project-level READY means is a product decision about submission semantics, not a defect. Both panels do surface their own state truthfully, so the UI is not misrepresenting the backend. Raised for the owner as a decision.

explicitly_not_caused_by.OCR_RECOGNITION: PaddleOCR read the meaningful content of every document that reached it at mean line confidence 0.82-0.96. Across the round, zero fixes changed the OCR model, the language model or the recognition settings. Where text was wrong it was wrong by one or two characters at low source resolution, not systematically.
explicitly_not_caused_by.CLASSIFICATION: After the routing fix, all 7 documents classified correctly (100%). No classifier change was needed or made. The filename is still excluded from the haystack.
explicitly_not_caused_by.ROW_GROUPING: Re-tested. Row grouping correctly rebuilt every letter-spaced label observed, including '성 명 :' split across boxes and '재 학 증 명 서' across five. No change was made to layout.py in this round.
